en.B: Moses summoned all Israel and said to them, "You yourselves have seen everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} did before your eyes in the land of Egypt to Pharaoh, to all his officials and to his whole land,

am.L: ሙሴም እስራኤልን ሁሉ ጠርቶ እንዲህ አላቸው፦ «{{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} በግብፅ ምድር በፈርዖንና በባሪያዎቹ ሁሉ፣ በምድሩም ሁሉ ላይ በዓይናችሁ ፊት ያደረገውን ሁሉ እናንተ አይታችኋል፤

am.R: ሙሴ የእስራኤልን ሕዝብ ሁሉ ሰብስቦ እንዲህ አላቸው፦ «{{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} በግብፅ ያደረገውን ሁሉ በገዛ ዓይናችሁ አይታችኋል። በፈርዖን፣ በሹማምንቱ ሁሉና በአገሩ ሁሉ ላይ ያደረገውን አይታችኋል።

decisions.choice: verse numbers: in many Bibles this verse is 29:2
decisions.reason: This translation numbers verses as the Hebrew text does. In the Hebrew text the verse before this one (28:69) closes chapter 28, and this verse opens chapter 29; many Bibles number that verse 29:1 and this one 29:2, so 29:1-28 here is 29:2-29 there. The words are the same; only the numbers differ.

decisions.choice: and said to them: the start of Moses' last long speech
decisions.reason: A short narrative line brings Moses before the people again, and his words begin with "You have seen". They run without a break to the end of chapter 30 (30:20). The speech calls Israel to enter the covenant made in the land of Moab (28:69), recalling what God has done, warning of what disobedience will bring, and ending with the choice between life and death (30:15-20).

decisions.choice: you, you have seen: the pronoun is stressed
decisions.reason: The verb already says "you have seen"; the added pronoun puts weight on it: you yourselves, and no one else, were witnesses. Most of the adults who left Egypt had died in the wilderness (2:14-16), but the people are addressed as one nation that saw God act, as in 5:3 and 11:7.

decisions.choice: what the LORD did in Egypt: the plagues and the rescue at the sea
decisions.reason: The words recall the signs and plagues of Exodus 7-12 and the drowning of Pharaoh's army in Exodus 14, which struck Pharaoh, his court and his land alike (Exodus 7:29; 10:6). Moses has made the same appeal before (4:34; 7:18-19; 11:3-4).

decisions.choice: officials
decisions.reason: The word usually means "servant" or "slave". With a king it names the members of his court, the men who served him in government (Exodus 7:10; 10:7). Literal keeps "servants"; Balanced and Readable say "officials".

decisions.choice: Moïse appela (L), convoqua (B), a réuni (R); vous avez vu (all levels)
decisions.reason: The narrator's frame is in the passé simple at Literal and Balanced and the passé composé at Readable (French style guide, section 3). Moses' own retelling of the past, which runs from here to the end of chapter 30, is in the passé composé at every level, as in the earlier speeches of Deuteronomy.

decisions.choice: officiers
decisions.reason: With a king the word names the men of his court who served him in government; "officiers" covers both his officials and his army leaders, who shared in the plagues and the defeat at the sea. Literal keeps "serviteurs", as the English Literal keeps "servants".

decisions.choice: "Chính các ngươi" for the stressed "you, you"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese stresses a pronoun with "chính"; repeating it would read as a slip.

decisions.choice: "신하"
decisions.reason: Pharaoh's servants are his court officials; "신하" is the Korean word for a king's servants, as the term sheet's "바로" for Pharaoh.

decisions.choice: Vocês, vocês viram (L); Vocês mesmos viram (B)
decisions.reason: The added pronoun stresses that these people themselves were witnesses (m3). Literal repeats it as the Hebrew does; Balanced says "vocês mesmos", the ordinary Portuguese stress. Pharaoh's servants are "oficiais" at Balanced and Readable, as in Exodus 10:7, and "Faraó" goes without an article as a name, as there.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Amharic
decisions.reason: The English of this chapter capitalises pronouns for God under the deity_pronoun setting. Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the Amharic has nothing for that setting to change and carries no deity_pronoun spans.

decisions.choice: Pharaoh's servants: "ባሪያዎቹ" (Literal), "ሹማምንቱ" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As settled for the Pentateuch: the king's men are his officials, and Balanced and Readable name them so.

decisions.choice: trials: tests of strength, the plagues that put Pharaoh to the test
decisions.reason: The word means a testing or proving. Here, as in 4:34 and 7:19, it names the plagues that tested Pharaoh and showed who held power over Egypt. The same word can be used of God testing Israel (8:2), but here the object is Egypt.

decisions.choice: signs and wonders: the plagues as proofs of God's power
decisions.reason: A sign points to and confirms a message; a wonder is a startling event (6:22; 7:19; Exodus 7:3). Together they name the plagues as acts that proved the LORD was God over Egypt and its gods.

decisions.choice: the verse spells out "all that the LORD did" in verse 1
decisions.reason: The verse has no verb of its own. It stands beside "all that the LORD did" in verse 1 and names what that was. "Your eyes" here is singular, the nation addressed as one person, after the plural of verse 1.

decisions.choice: You saw ... God put them through
decisions.reason: Readable repeats "you saw" and says who did the testing and who was tested, so that the verse can stand as sentences of its own. The verse itself has only the nouns.

decisions.choice: miracles
decisions.reason: Readable says "miracles" for "wonders", the common word for an amazing act that comes from God, as in 13:2.

decisions.choice: tus ojos (singular)
decisions.reason: After the plural of verse 1, "your eyes" here is singular in Hebrew: the nation is addressed as one person. Spanish follows the Hebrew number at every level, as in the rest of Deuteronomy, so this verse has "tú" and no plural_you span.

decisions.choice: "시험"
decisions.reason: The word is "tests", the plagues that put Pharaoh to the test; Korean keeps the word rather than naming the plagues.

decisions.choice: os teus olhos (L); vocês viram (B, R); as grandes provas
decisions.reason: "Your eyes" is singular after the plural of verse 1 (m3). Literal follows the Hebrew number word by word; Balanced keeps "vocês", since verses 1-2 are one sentence, and Readable goes on with the "vocês" of verse 1. "Provas" for the trials, as in 7:19.

decisions.choice: a heart to know: a mind able to understand
decisions.reason: In Hebrew the heart is the seat of thought and will more than of feeling. A heart to know is an understanding mind, able to grasp what God's acts mean (8:5; Proverbs 2:2).

decisions.choice: the LORD has not given: understanding is a gift Israel has not yet received
decisions.reason: Israel saw the wonders with their own eyes (verses 1-2), and still they did not truly understand them, as their complaining and rebellion in the wilderness showed (9:7, 24). Moses traces this to God, who had not yet given them this understanding. The same thought comes in Isaiah 6:9-10, and Paul quotes this verse in Romans 11:8. In 30:6 Moses promises that God will one day circumcise their hearts so that they love him.

decisions.choice: until this day: up to now, with a hint that it may change today
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean that the lack has lasted up to the present and still lasts, or it can mark today, the day of the covenant in Moab, as the turning point when Israel is called to understand. The verse states the past and present plainly and leaves the future open.

decisions.choice: an understanding mind / minds that understand
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "mind" for "heart", since the verse is about understanding, not feeling. Literal keeps "heart".

decisions.choice: really see ... really hear
decisions.reason: Readable adds "really": they had eyes and ears, and had seen and heard, but had not grasped what they saw and heard. The verse makes the point by contrast with verse 2.

decisions.choice: "የሚያስተውል ልብ፣ የሚያዩ ዓይኖችና የሚሰሙ ጆሮዎች" kept close to the wording of Romans 11:8 ("የማያዩ ዓይኖችንና የማይሰሙ ጆሮዎችን")
decisions.reason: Paul echoes this verse in Romans 11:8, but in his own form (God gave eyes that do not see). The Hebrew here says the LORD has not given seeing eyes, so the Amharic follows the Hebrew and keeps only the shared nouns and verbs.

decisions.choice: I led you: Moses speaks God's words in the first person
decisions.reason: Moses has been speaking of the LORD as "he" (verse 3), but here "I" is the LORD himself, as verse 5 makes clear: "that you may know that I am the LORD your God." Moses speaks as the LORD's spokesman and passes on God's own words without saying "the LORD says". The prophets often move in the same way between their own voice and God's. The speech returns to Moses' own voice in verse 6 ("to meet us").

decisions.choice: clothes and sandals that did not wear out
decisions.reason: Moses made the same point in 8:4: God's care in the wilderness was so complete that the people's clothes lasted all forty years. Nehemiah 9:21 recalls it in a prayer. The forty years recall Numbers 14:33-34.

decisions.choice: your garments ... your sandal: plural, then singular
decisions.reason: "Your garments" is addressed to the people as many; "your sandal" and "your foot" to the people as one, each person or the whole nation. Deuteronomy often moves between the two without a change of meaning.

decisions.choice: clothes ... sandals ... feet
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the ordinary plurals for all the people; Literal keeps the singular "sandal" and "foot" of the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: desert
decisions.reason: Readable says "desert", the everyday word for this dry land with few people. Literal and Balanced keep "wilderness".

decisions.choice: vos vêtements ... ta sandale / tes sandales
decisions.reason: French keeps the Hebrew move from plural ("your garments") to singular ("your sandal", "your foot") at every level, as Deuteronomy does throughout. Readable puts the sandals and feet in the plural, as the English does, but keeps the singular "tu".

decisions.choice: "Ta" and "các ngươi" in verses 4-5, where Moses speaks the LORD's words in the first person
decisions.reason: The meaning note says the "I" here is God (verse 5: "I am the LORD your God"); Vietnamese marks God speaking to Israel with "Ta" and "các ngươi", as the settled choice for God's address to Israel.

decisions.choice: "주님께서는 ... 인도하셨습니다" for God's "I led you"
decisions.reason: Here Moses speaks in God's own voice. In the polite 합쇼체 that Moses uses at Readable, a first-person pronoun would sound like Moses himself, so Readable names the Lord, as Deuteronomy 7:4 does; Literal and Balanced keep "나".

decisions.choice: as roupas de vocês ... a tua sandália ... teu pé (L); vocês throughout (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "your garments" in the plural and "your sandal", "your foot" in the singular (m3). Literal keeps both numbers; Balanced and Readable keep one form of address in the sentence, "vocês", with plural sandals and feet as the English does. The "eu" is the LORD speaking through Moses (m1).

am.R: የምትበሉት እንጀራ፣ የምትጠጡትም የወይን ጠጅ ወይም ጠላ አልነበራችሁም። ይህን ያደረግኩት እኔ አምላካችሁ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} መሆኔን እንድታውቁ ነው።

decisions.choice: bread, wine and strong drink: the food of farmers, which Israel did not have
decisions.reason: Bread is grain grown in fields; wine and strong drink come from vineyards and orchards. A people on the move in the wilderness had none of these. They lived instead on the manna God sent and the water he gave (8:3, 15-16), so their food each day came from God, not from their own fields.

decisions.choice: strong drink: an alcoholic drink other than wine
decisions.reason: The word names an intoxicating drink, probably beer made from grain, or a drink made from dates or other fruit. It is paired with wine in the laws of the priests and the Nazirite (Leviticus 10:9; Numbers 6:3) and in 14:26.

decisions.choice: so that you may know that I am the LORD your God
decisions.reason: The forty years without ordinary food were meant to teach Israel who their God was. This is the purpose stated for the plagues in Exodus (Exodus 6:7; 10:2; 16:12), and here it is applied to Israel's own life in the wilderness. As in verse 4, the "I" is the LORD.

decisions.choice: beer
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "beer", the nearest common drink; Literal keeps "strong drink". The exact drink is not certain (see the meaning note).

decisions.choice: I did this so that
decisions.reason: Readable begins a new sentence for the purpose and supplies "I did this", which the Hebrew leaves to be understood from verse 4.

decisions.choice: "독한 술"
decisions.reason: An alcoholic drink other than wine; Korean keeps the general "독한 술", where the English Balanced and Readable say "beer".

decisions.choice: "የሚያሰክር መጠጥ" (strong drink) at Literal; "ጠላ" (home-brewed grain beer) at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: "ጠላ" is the Ethiopian grain beer and the natural pair with wine in Amharic; "ቢራ" would suggest a factory drink.

records.literal_gloss: And you came to the place the this, and came out Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of the Bashan to meet us for battle, and we struck them.

en.L: And you came to this place, and Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan came out to meet us for battle, and we struck them down.
en.B: Then you arrived at this place, and Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan marched out to fight us, but we defeated them.
en.R: When you came to this place, King Sihon of Heshbon and King Og of Bashan marched out to fight us. But we beat them.

es.L: Y {{plural_you:llegaron|llegasteis}} a este lugar, y Sijón, rey de Hesbón, y Og, rey de Basán, salieron a nuestro encuentro para la batalla, y los abatimos.
es.B: Luego {{plural_you:llegaron|llegasteis}} a este lugar, y Sijón, rey de Hesbón, y Og, rey de Basán, salieron a pelear contra nosotros, pero los vencimos.
es.R: Cuando {{plural_you:llegaron|llegasteis}} a este lugar, el rey Sijón de Hesbón y el rey Og de Basán salieron a pelear contra nosotros. Pero los vencimos.

fr.L: Et vous êtes venus en ce lieu, et Sihon, roi de Heshbon, et Og, roi du Bashân, sont sortis à notre rencontre pour la bataille, et nous les avons battus.
fr.B: Puis vous êtes arrivés en ce lieu, et Sihon, roi de Heshbon, et Og, roi du Bashân, se sont mis en marche pour nous combattre, mais nous les avons vaincus.
fr.R: Quand vous êtes arrivés ici, Sihon, le roi de Heshbon, et Og, le roi du Bashân, sont partis en guerre contre nous. Mais nous les avons battus.

sw.L: Nanyi mlifika mahali hapa, na Sihoni mfalme wa Heshboni na Ogu mfalme wa Bashani wakatoka kutukabili kwa vita, nasi tukawapiga.
sw.B: Kisha mlifika mahali hapa, na Sihoni mfalme wa Heshboni na Ogu mfalme wa Bashani wakatoka kupigana nasi, lakini tukawashinda.
sw.R: Mlipofika mahali hapa, Mfalme Sihoni wa Heshboni na Mfalme Ogu wa Bashani walitoka kupigana nasi. Lakini tuliwashinda.

vi.B: Rồi anh em đến nơi này, và Si-hôn vua Hết-bôn cùng Óc vua Ba-san kéo quân ra đánh chúng ta, nhưng chúng ta đã đánh bại họ.

ko.B: 그 뒤에 너희가 이곳에 이르렀을 때에 헤스본 왕 시혼과 바산 왕 옥이 우리와 싸우려고 나왔으나, 우리가 그들을 물리쳤다.

pt.L: E vocês chegaram a este lugar, e saíram Seom, rei de Hesbom, e Ogue, rei de Basã, ao nosso encontro para a batalha, e nós os ferimos.
pt.B: Depois vocês chegaram a este lugar, e Seom, rei de Hesbom, e Ogue, rei de Basã, saíram para lutar contra nós, mas nós os derrotamos.
pt.R: Quando vocês chegaram a este lugar, o rei Seom, de Hesbom, e o rei Ogue, de Basã, vieram lutar contra nós. Mas nós vencemos os dois.

am.L: ወደዚህም ስፍራ መጣችሁ፤ የሐሴቦን ንጉሥ ሴዎንና የባሳን ንጉሥ ዐግ ሊዋጉን ሊገናኙን ወጡ፤ መታናቸውም።

decisions.choice: Sihon and Og: the two kings east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: The story is told in 2:26-3:11 and Numbers 21:21-35. Sihon the Amorite ruled from Heshbon, north of the Arnon; Og ruled Bashan, the high plain north of the Yarmuk. Their defeat was Israel's first conquest and a pledge of what God would do west of the Jordan (3:21-22; 31:4).

decisions.choice: you came ... to meet us ... we struck them: the speaker joins the people
decisions.reason: Moses moves from "you" to "us" and "we". He speaks again in his own voice (after the LORD's "I" in verses 4-5) and counts himself with the people who fought. "This place" is the plains of Moab across from Jericho, where Moses is speaking (1:5; 28:69; 34:1).

decisions.choice: came out to fight against us
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say the plain sense of "came out to meet us for battle": the kings marched out to fight. Literal keeps the idiom.

decisions.choice: "chúng ta" (inclusive "we") when Moses counts himself with the people
decisions.reason: Moses and his hearers fought together; Vietnamese inclusive "chúng ta" says so.

decisions.choice: "헤스본", "시혼", "바산", "옥"
decisions.reason: The names as the Pentateuch term sheet gives them (Sihon, Og, Bashan) and the usual Protestant form of Heshbon.

en.L: And we took their land and gave it as an inheritance to the Reubenites and to the Gadites and to the half-tribe of the Manassites.
en.B: We took their land and handed it over to the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh as their inheritance.
en.R: We took their land and gave it to the tribes of Reuben and Gad and to half the tribe of Manasseh to be their own.

decisions.choice: the land given to two and a half tribes
decisions.reason: Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh asked for the lands east of the Jordan and received them on condition that their fighting men crossed over with the others (Numbers 32; 3:12-20 here). The land already won shows that God keeps his promises, which is why it is mentioned before the call to keep the covenant in verse 8.

decisions.choice: inheritance: land held as a lasting family possession
decisions.reason: The word names property passed down within a family or tribe. Israel's land was its inheritance from God, shared out by tribe and clan and meant to stay in the family for good (4:21; 12:9; Numbers 26:52-56).

decisions.choice: the half-tribe of Manasseh
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the tribe, Manasseh, as the people are named elsewhere (3:13); the Hebrew here has "the Manassite", the name of the people. Literal keeps "Manassites".

decisions.choice: to be their own
decisions.reason: Readable says what "as an inheritance" means: the land became theirs to keep. The meaning note explains the word.

decisions.choice: "ርስት" for inheritance (naḥalah)
decisions.reason: As ruled for the whole Pentateuch: naḥalah is "ርስት"; "possession" (ʾaḥuzzah, yerushah) is kept apart as "ይዞታ". Readable says "to be their own".

am.L: እንግዲህ የምታደርጉትን ሁሉ ታከናውኑ ዘንድ የዚህን ቃል ኪዳን ቃሎች ጠብቁ፤ አድርጓቸውም።
am.B: ስለዚህ በምታደርጉት ነገር ሁሉ እንዲሳካላችሁ የዚህን ቃል ኪዳን ቃሎች ጠብቁ፤ ፈጽሟቸውም።
am.R: ስለዚህ ይህ ቃል ኪዳን የሚለውን ሁሉ ታዘዙ። ያን ጊዜ በምታደርጉት ሁሉ ይሳካላችኋል።

decisions.choice: the words of this covenant: the terms of the covenant made in Moab
decisions.reason: "This covenant" is the one named in 28:69, made in the land of Moab in addition to the one at Horeb. Its words are the laws and warnings Moses has given in this book. To keep them is to watch over them with care, and to do them is to carry them out.

decisions.choice: prosper: act wisely and so succeed
decisions.reason: The verb means both to act with insight and to have success as a result (Joshua 1:7-8; 1 Kings 2:3). Doing the covenant is the wise course, and it leads to things going well.

decisions.choice: and you shall keep: so, then; the call that follows from verses 1-7
decisions.reason: The verb form looks forward and draws a conclusion from what Israel has seen. Because God has done all this, Israel is to keep his covenant.

decisions.choice: terms
decisions.reason: Balanced says "terms" for "words": the words of a covenant are what it binds each side to. Literal keeps "words"; Readable says "everything this covenant says".

decisions.choice: les clauses
decisions.reason: "Clauses" is the ordinary French word for what a treaty or contract binds each side to, which is what the "words" of a covenant are. Literal keeps "paroles".

decisions.choice: esta aliança (every level)
decisions.reason: For chapters 29-30: the covenant made in the land of Moab (28:69; m1) is "a aliança" at every level, the word Deuteronomy uses for God's covenant with Israel (7:9; 8:18). Readable keeps it too: "acordo" is kept for treaties between peoples (7:2).

es.R: Hoy todos {{plural_you:ustedes están|vosotros estáis}} aquí, de pie ante {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}}. fr.L: Vous vous tenez aujourd’hui, vous tous, devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu : vos chefs, vos tribus, vos anciens et vos préposés, tout homme d’Israël,
fr.B: Vous vous tenez tous aujourd’hui devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu : les chefs de vos tribus, vos anciens et vos préposés, tous les hommes d’Israël,
fr.R: Aujourd’hui, vous êtes tous là, debout devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu. Les chefs de vos tribus, vos anciens, vos responsables et tous les hommes d’Israël sont ici.

sw.L: Ninyi mmesimama leo, nyote, mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu: wakuu wenu, makabila yenu, wazee wenu na wasimamizi wenu, kila mwanamume wa Israeli,
sw.B: Nyote mmesimama leo mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu: viongozi wa makabila yenu, wazee wenu na wasimamizi wenu, wanaume wote wa Israeli,
sw.R: Leo nyote mmesimama hapa mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu. Viongozi wa makabila yenu, wazee wenu, maafisa wenu na wanaume wote wa Israeli wako hapa.

vi.L: Hôm nay tất cả các ngươi đang đứng trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của các ngươi: các thủ lãnh của các ngươi, các chi tộc của các ngươi, các trưởng lão của các ngươi và các viên chức của các ngươi, mọi người nam Y-sơ-ra-ên,
vi.B: Hôm nay tất cả anh em đang đứng trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em: các thủ lãnh chi tộc, các trưởng lão và các viên chức của anh em, tất cả đàn ông Y-sơ-ra-ên,
vi.R: Hôm nay tất cả anh em đang đứng trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em. Các thủ lãnh chi tộc, các trưởng lão, các viên chức và tất cả đàn ông Y-sơ-ra-ên đều có mặt ở đây.

ko.L: 너희는 오늘 너희 모두가 너희 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에 서 있다. 너희 우두머리들, 너희 지파들, 너희 장로들과 너희 관리들, 이스라엘의 모든 사람,
ko.B: 오늘 너희는 모두 너희 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에 서 있다. 너희 지파의 지도자들과 장로들과 관리들과 이스라엘의 모든 남자들,
ko.R: 오늘 여러분은 모두 여러분의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에 서 있습니다. 여러분의 지파 지도자들과 장로들과 관리들과 이스라엘의 모든 남자들이 여기에 있습니다.

pt.L: Vocês estão de pé hoje, todos vocês, diante {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, o Deus de vocês: os cabeças de vocês, as tribos de vocês, os anciãos de vocês e os oficiais de vocês, todo homem de Israel,
pt.B: Todos vocês estão hoje diante {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, o Deus de vocês: os líderes das suas tribos, os seus anciãos e os seus oficiais, todos os homens de Israel,
pt.R: Hoje todos vocês estão aqui, diante {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, o Deus de vocês. Estão aqui os líderes das tribos, os anciãos, os oficiais e todos os homens de Israel.

am.L: እናንተ ሁላችሁ ዛሬ በአምላካችሁ {{divine_name:በእግዚአብሔር|በያህዌ}} ፊት ቆማችኋል፤ አለቆቻችሁ፣ ነገዶቻችሁ፣ ሽማግሌዎቻችሁና ሹሞቻችሁ፣ የእስራኤል ሰው ሁሉ፣
am.B: እናንተ ሁላችሁ ዛሬ በአምላካችሁ {{divine_name:በእግዚአብሔር|በያህዌ}} ፊት ቆማችኋል፤ የነገዶቻችሁ አለቆች፣ ሽማግሌዎቻችሁና ሹሞቻችሁ፣ የእስራኤል ወንዶች ሁሉ፣
am.R: ዛሬ ሁላችሁም በአምላካችሁ {{divine_name:በእግዚአብሔር|በያህዌ}} ፊት ቆማችኋል። የነገድ አለቆቻችሁ፣ ሽማግሌዎቻችሁ፣ ሹሞቻችሁና የእስራኤል ወንዶች ሁሉ እዚህ አሉ።

decisions.choice: standing: taking a set place, presenting yourselves
decisions.reason: The verb is used of people who take their place for a solemn occasion, as Israel stood at the foot of Mount Sinai (Exodus 19:17) or as the tribes presented themselves before the LORD (Joshua 24:1; 1 Samuel 10:19). The whole people are assembled for a covenant ceremony.

decisions.choice: your heads, your tribes: probably the heads of your tribes
alternatives: the heads of your tribes, as the Greek translation reads
decisions.reason: The Hebrew lists "your heads, your tribes" side by side, which reads oddly in a list of people. It is most likely a way of naming the leaders by tribe, and the ancient Greek translation has "the heads of your tribes". Some take the words as two items, leaders and the tribes as a whole. The meaning differs little: all Israel, led by its chiefs.

decisions.choice: the sentence runs on to verse 12
decisions.reason: Verses 9-12 are one sentence in Hebrew: it names everyone who stands there (verses 9-10) and says why they stand there, to enter the covenant (verses 11-12).

decisions.choice: officials: officers who kept records and carried out orders
decisions.reason: The word names men who helped the elders and judges, keeping lists and seeing that decisions were carried out (1:15; 16:18; 20:5).

decisions.choice: the leaders of your tribes / your tribal leaders
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow the likely sense of "your heads, your tribes" (see the meaning note). Literal keeps the two words as they stand.

decisions.choice: two sentences
decisions.reason: Readable ends the sentence after "before the LORD your God" and adds "are here" so that the list of those present can stand as a sentence. "All the men of Israel" names the men, since women and children follow in verse 10.

decisions.choice: "ሹሞች" for the officials (shoterim)
decisions.reason: The shoterim kept records and carried out orders; "ሹም" is an appointed official, and keeps them apart from the "አለቆች" (heads) and the "ሽማግሌዎች" (elders) in the same list.

source.text: טַפְּכֶ֣ם נְשֵׁיכֶ֔ם וְגֵ֣רְךָ֔ אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּקֶ֣רֶב מַחֲנֶ֑יךָ מֵחֹטֵ֣ב עֵצֶ֔יךָ עַ֖ד שֹׁאֵ֥ב מֵימֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: your little ones, your wives, and your sojourner who [is] in [the] midst of your camps, from [the] cutter of your wood to [the] drawer of your water,

en.L: your little ones, your wives, and your sojourner who [is] in the midst of your camps, from the one who cuts your wood to the one who draws your water,
en.B: your children, your wives, and the outsiders living in your camps, from those who cut your wood to those who draw your water,
en.R: Your children and your wives are here too. So are the outsiders who live in your camps, even the ones who cut your firewood and carry your water.

es.L: {{plural_you:sus pequeños|vuestros pequeños}}, {{plural_you:sus mujeres|vuestras mujeres}} y tu inmigrante que [está] en medio de tus campamentos, desde el que corta tu leña hasta el que saca tu agua,
es.B: {{plural_you:sus niños|vuestros niños}}, {{plural_you:sus mujeres|vuestras mujeres}} y los extranjeros que viven en tus campamentos, desde el que te corta la leña hasta el que te saca el agua,
es.R: También están aquí {{plural_you:sus hijos|vuestros hijos}} y {{plural_you:sus esposas|vuestras esposas}}. Y lo mismo los extranjeros que viven en tus campamentos, hasta los que te cortan la leña y te acarrean el agua.

fr.L: vos petits, vos femmes, et ton immigré qui [est] au milieu de tes camps, depuis celui qui coupe ton bois jusqu’à celui qui puise ton eau,
fr.B: vos enfants, vos femmes et l’étranger qui vit dans tes camps, depuis celui qui te coupe le bois jusqu’à celui qui te puise l’eau,
fr.R: Vos enfants et vos femmes sont là aussi. Les étrangers qui vivent dans ton camp sont là eux aussi, même ceux qui coupent ton bois de chauffage et portent ton eau.

sw.L: watoto wenu wadogo, wake zenu, na mgeni wako aliye katikati ya kambi zako, tangu yule akukatiaye kuni hadi yule akutekeaye maji,
sw.B: watoto wenu, wake zenu, na wageni wanaoishi kambini mwako, tangu wanaokukatia kuni hadi wanaokutekea maji,
sw.R: Watoto wenu na wake zenu wako hapa pia. Vivyo hivyo wageni wanaoishi kambini mwako, hata wale wanaokukatia kuni na kukuchotea maji.

vi.L: con trẻ các ngươi, vợ các ngươi, và ngoại kiều của ngươi ở giữa trại quân ngươi, từ người chặt củi cho ngươi đến người múc nước cho ngươi,
vi.B: con cái và vợ của anh em, cùng các ngoại kiều sống trong trại quân anh em, từ người chặt củi cho đến người múc nước cho anh em,
vi.R: Con cái và vợ của anh em cũng có mặt. Các ngoại kiều sống trong khu trại của anh em cũng vậy, kể cả những người chặt củi và gánh nước cho anh em.

ko.L: 너희 어린것들과 너희 아내들과 네 진 가운데 있는 네 나그네, 곧 네 나무를 패는 자부터 네 물을 긷는 자까지,
ko.B: 너희 아이들과 아내들과 너희 진 가운데 사는 나그네들, 곧 너희를 위해 나무를 패는 사람부터 물을 긷는 사람까지,
ko.R: 여러분의 아이들과 아내들도 여기에 있습니다. 여러분의 진 가운데 사는 외국 사람들도 있고, 여러분을 위해 장작을 패고 물을 길어 오는 사람들도 있습니다.

pt.L: as crianças de vocês, as mulheres de vocês, e o teu imigrante que [está] no meio dos teus acampamentos, desde o que corta a tua lenha até o que tira a tua água,
pt.B: os seus filhos pequenos, as suas mulheres e os imigrantes que vivem no acampamento de vocês, desde quem corta a lenha até quem tira a água para vocês,
pt.R: Os filhos e as mulheres de vocês também estão aqui. Também estão aqui os estrangeiros que moram nos acampamentos de vocês, até os que cortam lenha e carregam água para vocês.

am.L: ሕፃናቶቻችሁ፣ ሚስቶቻችሁ፣ በሰፈርህም መካከል ያለው መጻተኛህ፣ እንጨትህን ከሚቆርጠው ጀምሮ ውኃህን እስከሚቀዳው ድረስ፣
am.B: ልጆቻችሁ፣ ሚስቶቻችሁና በሰፈራችሁ የሚኖሩ መጻተኞች፣ እንጨት ከሚቆርጡላችሁ ጀምሮ ውኃ እስከሚቀዱላችሁ ድረስ፣
am.R: ልጆቻችሁና ሚስቶቻችሁም እዚህ አሉ። በሰፈራችሁ የሚኖሩ ስደተኞችም፣ የማገዶ እንጨት የሚቆርጡላችሁና ውኃ የሚቀዱላችሁ እንኳ እዚህ አሉ።

decisions.choice: little ones, wives, sojourner: everyone in the community, not only the men
decisions.reason: The covenant is made with the whole community. Women and children are named, as at the reading of the law in 31:12 and Joshua 8:35. The sojourner is a foreigner who lives among Israel without land of his own; he too is bound to the covenant and protected by it (10:18-19; 24:17).

decisions.choice: from the one who cuts your wood to the one who draws your water: down to the lowest workers
decisions.reason: Cutting wood and drawing water were the hardest and lowest jobs in a camp or village. To name them is to say that no one is left out, however humble. The Gibeonites were later made woodcutters and water carriers for Israel (Joshua 9:21-27).

decisions.choice: your sojourner ... your camps: the nation addressed as one
decisions.reason: From here the address turns singular ("your sojourner", "your camps"), and it stays singular through verse 12: the people are spoken to as one nation entering the covenant.

decisions.choice: outsiders living in your camps
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "outsider", as in 1:16: a foreigner living among Israel. Literal keeps "sojourner". The singular stands for the whole group, so Balanced and Readable use the plural.

decisions.choice: separate sentences with "are here too"
decisions.reason: Readable continues its own sentences from verse 9 and supplies "are here" and "so are". It says "firewood" and "carry", the everyday words for this work.

decisions.choice: o teu imigrante ... teus acampamentos (L); vocês through verse 12 (B, R); o imigrante (L, B), os estrangeiros que moram (R)
decisions.reason: Here the Hebrew turns to the singular and stays there through verse 12 (m3). Literal follows it word by word. At Balanced, verses 9-12 are one sentence that began with "vocês", so it keeps "vocês" to the end, as 12:1 does; Readable goes on in the same address. The ger is "o imigrante" (L, B) and "os estrangeiros que moram" among them (R), as 1:16 sets it.

source.text: לְעָבְרְךָ֗ בִּבְרִ֛ית יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ וּבְאָלָת֑וֹ אֲשֶׁר֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ כֹּרֵ֥ת עִמְּךָ֖ הַיּֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: for your passing into [the] covenant of Yahweh your God and into his oath, which Yahweh your God [is] cutting with you the day,

en.L: so that you may pass into the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} oath, which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is making with you today,
en.B: so that you may pass into the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and into the oath {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is making with you today,
en.R: You are here to enter into a covenant with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and to accept the solemn oath that goes with it. Today {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is making this covenant with you.

es.L: para que entres en el pacto {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} tu Dios y en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} juramento, que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios hace hoy contigo,
es.B: para que entres en el pacto {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} tu Dios y en el juramento que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} hace hoy contigo,
es.R: Estás aquí para entrar en un pacto con {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios y para aceptar el juramento solemne que lo acompaña. Hoy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios hace este pacto contigo.

fr.L: pour que tu entres dans l’alliance {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ton Dieu et dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} serment, que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu conclut avec toi aujourd’hui,
fr.B: pour que tu entres dans l’alliance {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ton Dieu et dans le serment qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} conclut avec toi aujourd’hui,
fr.R: Tu es ici pour entrer dans l’alliance avec {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu et pour accepter le serment solennel qui l’accompagne. Aujourd’hui, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu conclut cette alliance avec toi.

sw.L: ili uingie katika agano la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako, na katika kiapo {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}}, ambalo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako analifanya nawe leo,
sw.B: ili uingie katika agano la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako, na katika kiapo anachokifanya nawe leo,
sw.R: Uko hapa ili uingie katika agano na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako, na kukubali kiapo kizito kinachoambatana nalo. Leo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako anafanya agano hili nawe.

vi.L: để ngươi bước vào giao ước của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi và vào lời thề của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, mà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi đang lập với ngươi hôm nay,
vi.B: để anh em bước vào giao ước của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em và vào lời thề mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang lập với anh em hôm nay,
vi.R: Anh em có mặt ở đây để bước vào giao ước với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em và chấp nhận lời thề long trọng đi kèm giao ước ấy. Hôm nay {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em đang lập giao ước này với anh em.

ko.L: 네가 네 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 언약과 그분의 맹세 안으로 들어가게 하려는 것이니, 그것은 네 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 오늘 너와 맺으시는 것이다.
ko.B: 너희가 너희 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 언약에 들어가고, 그분께서 오늘 너희와 맺으시는 맹세에 참여하게 하려는 것이다.
ko.R: 여러분이 여기 모인 것은 여러분의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}와 언약을 맺고, 그 언약에 따르는 엄숙한 맹세를 받아들이기 위해서입니다. 오늘 여러분의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 여러분과 이 언약을 맺으십니다.

pt.L: para entrares na aliança {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, o teu Deus, e no {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} juramento, que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o teu Deus, está fazendo contigo hoje,

decisions.choice: pass into the covenant: enter it, become bound by it
alternatives: cross over into the covenant as into a land
decisions.reason: The verb means to cross over or pass through. With "covenant" it means to enter it and take on its obligations. The picture may come from a ceremony in which those making a covenant walked between the halves of animals cut in two (Genesis 15:9-17; Jeremiah 34:18-19). That ceremony is not described here.

decisions.choice: his oath: the sworn pledge that binds the covenant, with curses if it is broken
decisions.reason: The word means a solemn oath that calls down a curse on whoever breaks it. Here it is the oath that seals the covenant, and the same word is used for the curses of the covenant in verses 18-20. "His oath" is the oath sworn before him and enforced by him.

decisions.choice: is cutting: is making a covenant
decisions.reason: To make a covenant is literally to "cut" one, perhaps from the cutting of animals in the ceremony (see m1). The phrase is the ordinary way to say "make a covenant" (5:2-3; 28:69).

decisions.choice: making
decisions.reason: Every level says "making" for the verb "cut", since that is what the idiom means. The gloss keeps "cutting".

decisions.choice: You are here to ... accept the solemn oath that goes with it
decisions.reason: Readable begins a new sentence and supplies "You are here" and "accept". It says "solemn oath" to show that this oath carries a penalty, which verses 18-20 make plain.

decisions.choice: juramento (verses 11, 13, 18); maldición (verse 19)
decisions.reason: The one Hebrew word is a sworn oath that calls down a curse on whoever breaks it. Spanish says "juramento" where the covenant is sworn and "maldición" where the curses fall (verse 19), as the English does.

decisions.choice: serment (verses 11, 13, 18); malédiction (verse 19)
decisions.reason: The one Hebrew word is a sworn oath that calls down a curse on whoever breaks it. Like the English, French says "serment" where the covenant is sworn and "malédiction" where the curses fall (verse 19); Readable adds "solennel" to show that the oath carries a penalty.

decisions.choice: kiapo (verses 11, 13, 18); laana (verse 19)
decisions.reason: The one Hebrew word is a sworn oath that calls down a curse on whoever breaks it. Swahili says "kiapo" where the covenant is sworn and "laana" where the curses fall (verse 19), as the English does; Readable says "kiapo kizito", a weighty oath.

decisions.choice: "맹세"
decisions.reason: The sworn pledge that binds the covenant, with curses if it is broken; Korean keeps the one word "맹세" here and in verses 13 and 18 so that the reader sees it is the same oath, and verse 20 names the curses.

decisions.choice: entrar na aliança; o juramento (verses 11, 13, 18); a maldição where the English says "curse" (verses 19-20)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "pass into" a covenant means to enter it and take on its obligations (m1); Portuguese says "entrar na aliança" at every level, since "passar à aliança" is not Portuguese. The word for the sworn pledge (m2) is "juramento" where the English says "oath" and "maldição" where it says "curse", so that the Portuguese follows the same two senses.

decisions.choice: "መሐላ" for the covenant oath (ʾalah), here and in verses 13, 18; "እርግማን" where ʾalah names the curses themselves (verses 19-20; 30:7)
decisions.reason: The word is the sworn oath that carries its curses. Where the oath is taken, Amharic says "መሐላ"; where its penalties fall, "እርግማን", as the English does.

decisions.choice: his people, and he your God: the heart of the covenant
decisions.reason: These words are the covenant formula, the short summary of the bond between God and Israel: they belong to him, and he is their God (26:17-18; Exodus 6:7; Leviticus 26:12). Today in Moab that bond is confirmed for the generation about to enter the land.

decisions.choice: establish: set up, confirm
decisions.reason: The verb means to raise up or make stand, and so to confirm something already promised (8:18; 28:9). God made Israel his people at Sinai; here he confirms them as his people again.

decisions.choice: as he swore to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob
decisions.reason: God promised Abraham to be God to him and to his descendants after him (Genesis 17:7-8), and he repeated the promise to Isaac and to Jacob (Genesis 26:3-4; 28:13-15). The covenant in Moab keeps that promise.

decisions.choice: as he spoke to you: what God has said to Israel itself
decisions.reason: Besides the oath to the ancestors, God has spoken this promise to Israel directly, at Sinai and through Moses (26:18; Exodus 19:5-6).

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "ancestors" for "fathers", the forefathers of the nation named in the verse. Literal keeps "fathers".

decisions.choice: He wants to make you his own people
decisions.reason: Readable begins a new sentence, makes God the subject, and says "wants to" for the Hebrew "in order to", which states God's purpose in the covenant.

decisions.choice: o povo que pertence a ele (B); o povo dele (R)
decisions.reason: With "vocês" in the sentence, "o seu povo" could be read as "your people"; Balanced and Readable say whose people they are in words that cannot be mistaken (the covenant formula, m1).

decisions.choice: I am making: Moses speaks as the one who makes the covenant on the LORD's behalf
decisions.reason: In verse 11 it is the LORD who makes the covenant; here Moses says "I", and in verse 14 he says "the LORD our God", so the speaker is Moses. He acts as the LORD's go-between, setting out the covenant and calling the people into it, as at Horeb (5:5).

decisions.choice: not with you alone: the sentence runs on into verse 14
decisions.reason: The verse sets up a contrast that verse 14 completes: not with you alone, but also with those who are not here today.

decisions.choice: this oath: the sworn pledge of the covenant
decisions.reason: As in verse 11, the oath is the solemn pledge that binds the covenant and calls down its curses on those who break it.

decisions.choice: only with you who are here
decisions.reason: Readable adds "who are here" to prepare for verse 14, which names those who are not here.

es.R: Lo hago con todos nosotros, los que estamos aquí hoy de pie ante {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nuestro Dios. Y lo hago también con los que no están hoy aquí con nosotros.

fr.L: mais avec celui qui est ici avec nous, se tenant aujourd’hui devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} notre Dieu, et avec celui qui n’est pas ici avec nous aujourd’hui.
fr.B: mais avec ceux qui se tiennent ici avec nous aujourd’hui devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} notre Dieu, et aussi avec ceux qui ne sont pas ici avec nous aujourd’hui.
fr.R: Je la conclus avec nous tous qui nous tenons ici aujourd’hui devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} notre Dieu. Et je la conclus aussi avec ceux qui ne sont pas ici avec nous aujourd’hui.

sw.L: bali pamoja na yeye aliye hapa pamoja nasi, akisimama leo mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu, na pamoja na yeye asiye hapa pamoja nasi leo.

vi.B: nhưng với những người hôm nay đang đứng đây với chúng ta trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của chúng ta, và cũng với những người hôm nay không có mặt ở đây với chúng ta.
vi.R: Tôi lập giao ước với tất cả chúng ta là những người hôm nay đang đứng đây trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của chúng ta. Tôi cũng lập giao ước với những người hôm nay không có mặt ở đây với chúng ta.

ko.L: 오늘 여기 우리와 함께 우리 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에 서 있는 자와도, 오늘 여기 우리와 함께 있지 않은 자와도 [맺는 것이다].
ko.B: 오늘 여기 우리 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에 우리와 함께 서 있는 사람들뿐 아니라, 오늘 여기 우리와 함께 있지 않은 사람들과도 맺는 것이다.
ko.R: 저는 오늘 우리 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에 서 있는 우리 모두와 이 언약을 맺습니다. 그리고 오늘 여기 우리와 함께 있지 않은 사람들과도 이 언약을 맺습니다.

pt.L: mas com quem está aqui conosco, de pé hoje diante {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, o nosso Deus, e com quem não está aqui conosco hoje.
pt.B: mas com os que estão aqui conosco hoje, diante {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, o nosso Deus, e também com os que não estão aqui conosco hoje.
pt.R: Estou fazendo esta aliança com todos nós que estamos aqui hoje, diante {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, o nosso Deus. E estou fazendo esta aliança também com os que não estão aqui conosco hoje.

am.L: ነገር ግን ዛሬ በአምላካችን {{divine_name:በእግዚአብሔር|በያህዌ}} ፊት ከእኛ ጋር በዚህ ቆሞ ካለው ጋር፣ ዛሬም ከእኛ ጋር በዚህ ከሌለው ጋር ነው።
am.B: ነገር ግን ዛሬ በአምላካችን {{divine_name:በእግዚአብሔር|በያህዌ}} ፊት ከእኛ ጋር በዚህ ከቆሙት ጋር፣ ደግሞም ዛሬ ከእኛ ጋር በዚህ ከሌሉት ጋር ነው።
am.R: ዛሬ በአምላካችን {{divine_name:በእግዚአብሔር|በያህዌ}} ፊት እዚህ ከቆምነው ከሁላችን ጋር አደርገዋለሁ። ደግሞም ዛሬ ከእኛ ጋር እዚህ ከሌሉት ጋር አደርገዋለሁ።

decisions.choice: those not here today: the generations still to come
decisions.reason: The covenant binds not only the people present but those not yet born, their descendants. Verse 21 speaks of "the generation to come, your children who rise up after you", and 5:3 makes the same point the other way round: the covenant at Horeb was made "with us, all of us here alive today". Each generation stands under the covenant as if it had been there.

decisions.choice: whoever is here: one who is present
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses a word for "there is" with "him": "the one who is here". The singular names each person present, and together they are the whole assembly.

decisions.choice: I am making it with ... And I am also making it with
decisions.reason: Readable repeats the verb from verse 13 so that each sentence can stand on its own.

records.literal_gloss: For you, you know how we lived in [the] land of Egypt and how we passed through [the] midst of the nations which you passed through.

en.L: For you yourselves know how we lived in the land of Egypt and how we passed through the midst of the nations through which you passed.
en.B: You yourselves know how we lived in Egypt and how we made our way through the nations along the route you took.
en.R: You know how we lived in Egypt. You know how we traveled through the lands of other nations on our way here.

fr.B: Vous savez vous-mêmes comment nous avons vécu en Égypte et comment nous avons fait route à travers les nations, par le chemin que vous avez suivi.
fr.R: Vous savez comment nous avons vécu en Égypte. Vous savez comment nous avons traversé les pays d’autres nations pour arriver jusqu’ici.

pt.B: Vocês mesmos sabem como vivemos no Egito e como atravessamos o território das nações pelo caminho que vocês fizeram.

decisions.choice: for you know: the reason for the warning that follows
decisions.reason: The word "for" leads into verses 15-17. Israel knows the gods of Egypt and of the nations along the way, and has seen their idols (verse 16). That is why the warning against turning to them follows in verse 17.

decisions.choice: the nations you passed through: Edom, Moab, Ammon and the Amorites
decisions.reason: On the way from Egypt Israel passed by or through the lands of Edom, Moab and Ammon and the kingdoms of Sihon and Og (2:1-3:11; Numbers 20-21). At Baal-peor in Moab many Israelites had already joined in the worship of a foreign god (4:3; Numbers 25:1-3).

decisions.choice: on our way here
decisions.reason: Readable leaves out the repeated "which you passed through" and says instead that the journey led to where they now stand.

ko.L: 그리고 너희는 그들 가운데 있는 그들의 혐오스러운 것들과 그들의 우상들, 곧 나무와 돌과 은과 금을 보았다.
ko.B: 너희는 그들 가운데 있는 혐오스러운 것들, 곧 나무와 돌과 은과 금으로 만든 그들의 우상들을 보았다.

am.L: አስጸያፊ ነገሮቻቸውንና ጣዖቶቻቸውን፣ በመካከላቸው ያሉትን እንጨትንና ድንጋይን፣ ብርንና ወርቅን አያችሁ።

am.R: ከእንጨትና ከድንጋይ፣ ከብርና ከወርቅ የተሠሩ አስጸያፊ ጣዖቶቻቸውን አያችሁ።

decisions.choice: detestable things: objects of worship that God hates
decisions.reason: The word names something loathsome and filthy, and it is used most often of the idols of other nations and their worship (1 Kings 11:5, 7; 2 Kings 23:13). Moses calls them what they are in God's eyes.

decisions.choice: idols: a scornful word for false gods
decisions.reason: The word for idols here may come from a root meaning to roll, and it may have reminded hearers of a word for dung, so that it mocks the images as lumps of filth. It is used most often by Ezekiel (Ezekiel 6:4-6), and in the Torah also in Leviticus 26:30.

decisions.choice: wood and stone, silver and gold: images made by hand
decisions.reason: Idols were carved from wood or stone, or cast and overlaid with silver and gold. Moses stresses that they were made things, "the work of human hands, wood and stone" (4:28).

decisions.choice: disgusting idols
decisions.reason: Readable joins the two nouns into one phrase, since both name the idols, and says "disgusting" for "detestable". Literal and Balanced keep both nouns.

decisions.choice: "những vật đáng ghê tởm" for the detestable things, "thần tượng" for the scornful word for idols
decisions.reason: Plain modern words; "gớm ghiếc" is the older Bible word.

decisions.choice: as coisas detestáveis (L, B); repugnantes (R)
decisions.reason: This word for idols as loathsome things (m1) is not the to'evah that Deuteronomy renders "abominação" (7:25); Portuguese keeps the two apart, as the English does with "detestable" and "abomination".

source.text: פֶּן־יֵ֣שׁ בָּ֠כֶם אִ֣ישׁ אוֹ־אִשָּׁ֞ה א֧וֹ מִשְׁפָּחָ֣ה אוֹ־שֵׁ֗בֶט אֲשֶׁר֩ לְבָב֨וֹ פֹנֶ֤ה הַיּוֹם֙ מֵעִם֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ לָלֶ֣כֶת לַעֲבֹ֔ד אֶת־אֱלֹהֵ֖י הַגּוֹיִ֣ם הָהֵ֑ם פֶּן־יֵ֣שׁ בָּכֶ֗ם שֹׁ֛רֶשׁ פֹּרֶ֥ה רֹ֖אשׁ וְלַעֲנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Lest there be among you a man or a woman or a clan or a tribe whose heart [is] turning the day from with Yahweh our God, to go to serve [the] gods of the nations the those; lest there be among you a root bearing poison and wormwood.

en.L: [Beware] lest there be among you a man or a woman or a clan or a tribe whose heart is turning away today from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, to go and serve the gods of those nations; lest there be among you a root bearing poison and wormwood.
en.B: Make sure there is no man or woman, no clan or tribe among you, whose heart turns away today from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God and goes off to serve the gods of those nations. Let no root grow among you that bears poison and bitter fruit.
en.R: Make sure that no man or woman, no family or tribe among you, turns away from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God today to worship the gods of those nations. Such people are like a root that grows a poisonous and bitter plant.

es.L: [{{plural_you:Cuídense|Cuidaos}}] de que no haya entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} hombre ni mujer, ni clan ni tribu cuyo corazón se aparte hoy {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} nuestro Dios para ir a servir a los dioses de aquellas naciones; de que no haya entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} raíz que dé veneno y ajenjo.
es.B: {{plural_you:Asegúrense|Aseguraos}} de que no haya entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} hombre ni mujer, clan ni tribu, cuyo corazón se aparte hoy {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} nuestro Dios y se vaya a servir a los dioses de esas naciones. Que no crezca entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} ninguna raíz que dé veneno y fruto amargo.
es.R: {{plural_you:Asegúrense|Aseguraos}} de que nadie entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, ni hombre ni mujer, ni familia ni tribu, se aparte hoy {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} nuestro Dios para adorar a los dioses de esas naciones. Gente así es como una raíz que produce una planta venenosa y amarga.

fr.L: [Prenez garde] qu’il n’y ait parmi vous homme ou femme, clan ou tribu dont le cœur se détourne aujourd’hui {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} notre Dieu pour aller servir les dieux de ces nations ; qu’il n’y ait parmi vous aucune racine qui porte du poison et de l’absinthe.
fr.B: Veillez à ce qu’il n’y ait parmi vous ni homme ni femme, ni clan ni tribu, dont le cœur se détourne aujourd’hui {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} notre Dieu pour aller servir les dieux de ces nations. Qu’aucune racine ne pousse parmi vous, qui porte du poison et des fruits amers.
fr.R: Faites bien attention : que personne parmi vous, homme ou femme, famille ou tribu, ne se détourne aujourd’hui {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} notre Dieu pour adorer les dieux de ces nations. De telles personnes sont comme une racine qui donne une plante empoisonnée et amère.

sw.L: [Jihadharini] asiwepo kati yenu mwanamume au mwanamke, au ukoo au kabila, ambaye moyo wake unageuka leo kumwacha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu, aende kuitumikia miungu ya mataifa hayo; pasiwepo kati yenu mzizi uzaao sumu na pakanga.
sw.B: Hakikisheni kwamba hakuna kati yenu mwanamume au mwanamke, ukoo au kabila, ambaye moyo wake unamwacha leo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu na kwenda kuitumikia miungu ya mataifa hayo. Pasiwe kati yenu mzizi unaozaa sumu na matunda machungu.
sw.R: Hakikisheni kwamba hakuna mtu kati yenu, mwanamume au mwanamke, ukoo au kabila, atakayemwacha leo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu ili kuabudu miungu ya mataifa hayo. Watu kama hao ni kama mzizi unaotoa mmea wenye sumu na uchungu.

vi.L: [Hãy coi chừng] kẻo có giữa các ngươi một người nam hay một người nữ, một gia tộc hay một chi tộc mà lòng hôm nay quay khỏi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của chúng ta để đi phục vụ các thần của những dân tộc ấy; kẻo có giữa các ngươi một cái rễ sinh ra chất độc và ngải đắng.
vi.B: Hãy coi chừng, đừng để có người nam hay người nữ, gia tộc hay chi tộc nào giữa anh em mà hôm nay lòng quay khỏi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của chúng ta để đi phục vụ các thần của những dân tộc ấy. Đừng để giữa anh em mọc lên một cái rễ sinh ra trái độc và đắng.
vi.R: Hãy coi chừng, đừng để người nam hay người nữ, gia đình hay chi tộc nào giữa anh em hôm nay quay lưng lại với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của chúng ta mà đi thờ lạy các thần của những dân tộc ấy. Những người như vậy giống như một cái rễ mọc lên thành cây độc và đắng.

ko.L: 너희 가운데 남자나 여자나 가문이나 지파 가운데 오늘 마음이 우리 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}에게서 돌아서서 그 민족들의 신들을 섬기러 가는 자가 있지 않게 [조심하여라]. 너희 가운데 독초와 쑥을 맺는 뿌리가 있지 않게 [하여라].
ko.B: 너희 가운데 남자든 여자든, 어떤 가문이나 지파든, 오늘 우리 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}에게서 마음이 떠나 그 민족들의 신들을 섬기러 가는 일이 없도록 하여라. 너희 가운데 독과 쓴 열매를 맺는 뿌리가 자라지 않게 하여라.
ko.R: 여러분 가운데 어떤 남자나 여자, 어떤 집안이나 지파도 오늘 우리 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 떠나 그 민족들의 신들을 섬기지 않도록 조심하십시오. 그런 사람은 독이 있고 쓴 풀을 자라게 하는 뿌리와 같습니다.

pt.L: [Tenham cuidado] para que não haja entre vocês homem, ou mulher, ou clã, ou tribo, cujo coração se desvie hoje {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, o nosso Deus, para ir servir os deuses daquelas nações; para que não haja entre vocês uma raiz que produza veneno e absinto.
pt.B: Cuidem para que não haja entre vocês homem ou mulher, clã ou tribo, cujo coração se desvie hoje {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, o nosso Deus, e vá servir os deuses daquelas nações. Que não cresça entre vocês nenhuma raiz que dê fruto venenoso e amargo.
pt.R: Tenham cuidado para que nenhum homem ou mulher, nenhuma família ou tribo entre vocês se afaste hoje {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, o nosso Deus, para adorar os deuses daquelas nações. Gente assim é como uma raiz que faz crescer uma planta venenosa e amarga.

am.L: ዛሬ ልቡ ከአምላካችን {{divine_name:ከእግዚአብሔር|ከያህዌ}} ዘወር ብሎ የእነዚያን ሕዝቦች አማልክት ሊያገለግል የሚሄድ ወንድ ወይም ሴት ወይም ጎሳ ወይም ነገድ በመካከላችሁ እንዳይኖር፣ መርዝንና እሬትን የሚያፈራ ሥር በመካከላችሁ እንዳይኖር [ተጠንቀቁ]።
am.B: ዛሬ ልቡ ከአምላካችን {{divine_name:ከእግዚአብሔር|ከያህዌ}} ዘወር ብሎ የእነዚያን ሕዝቦች አማልክት ሊያገለግል የሚሄድ ወንድ ወይም ሴት፣ ጎሳ ወይም ነገድ በመካከላችሁ እንዳይኖር ተጠንቀቁ። መርዝና መራራ ፍሬ የሚያፈራ ሥር በመካከላችሁ አይብቀል።
am.R: ከእናንተ መካከል ማንም ወንድ ወይም ሴት፣ ቤተሰብ ወይም ነገድ ዛሬ ከአምላካችን {{divine_name:ከእግዚአብሔር|ከያህዌ}} ዘወር ብሎ የእነዚያን ሕዝቦች አማልክት እንዳያመልክ ተጠንቀቁ። እንደዚህ ያሉ ሰዎች መርዘኛና መራራ ተክል እንደሚያበቅል ሥር ናቸው።

decisions.choice: lest: a warning, beware that there is not
decisions.reason: The word means "so that not" or "lest". Here it stands at the start of the sentence without a verb before it and works as a warning: take care that there is no such person among you.

decisions.choice: whose heart turns away from the LORD: who inwardly stops being loyal to him
decisions.reason: The heart is the inner self, mind and will. A heart that turns from God has already left him before any act of worship of another god (11:16; 30:17). The danger can begin in one person and spread to a clan or a whole tribe.

decisions.choice: a root bearing poison and wormwood: a hidden source of deadly growth
decisions.reason: A root lies under the ground and is not seen, yet it bears fruit. The person who turns from God is pictured as such a root, whose fruit is poison for the whole people. "Poison" names a poisonous plant, perhaps the poppy or hemlock; wormwood is a plant known for its bitter taste (Amos 6:12; Jeremiah 9:14). The letter to the Hebrews draws on this verse (Hebrews 12:15).

decisions.choice: [Beware] lest
decisions.reason: Literal supplies "beware" in brackets, since the warning has no verb before "lest" in Hebrew.

decisions.choice: bitter fruit / bitter plant
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what wormwood is, a bitter plant, rather than its name. Literal keeps "wormwood".

decisions.choice: Such people are like a root
decisions.reason: Readable states the picture as a comparison and names who the root is, the people just described. The Hebrew sets the two warnings side by side and leaves the link to be seen.

decisions.choice: pakanga
decisions.reason: "Pakanga" is the name Swahili Bible readers know for wormwood, the bitter plant (it is the name of the star in Revelation 8:11). Literal keeps the plant's name, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable say what it is, something bitter.

decisions.choice: "ngải đắng" for wormwood
decisions.reason: The plant's usual Vietnamese name; B and R say "đắng" (bitter), as the English does.
Literal names the bitter plant, wormwood; Balanced and Readable say what it means, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "መርዝንና እሬትን የሚያፈራ ሥር" (Literal); "መራራ" (bitter) at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: Wormwood is named by the bitter plant Amharic readers know, "እሬት". Hebrews 12:15 echoes the verse as a "መራራ ሥር" in the Amharic New Testament; Balanced and Readable keep "መራራ" so the echo can be heard.

source.text: וְהָיָ֡ה בְּשָׁמְעוֹ֩ אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֨י הָֽאָלָ֜ה הַזֹּ֗את וְהִתְבָּרֵ֨ךְ בִּלְבָב֤וֹ לֵאמֹר֙ שָׁל֣וֹם יִֽהְיֶה־לִּ֔י כִּ֛י בִּשְׁרִר֥וּת לִבִּ֖י אֵלֵ֑ךְ לְמַ֛עַן סְפ֥וֹת הָרָוָ֖ה אֶת־הַצְּמֵאָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be, when he hears [the] words of the oath the this, and he blesses himself in his heart, saying, peace will be to me, though in [the] stubbornness of my heart I walk, so as to sweep away the watered with the thirsty.

en.L: And it will be, when he hears the words of this oath, that he will bless himself in his heart, saying, 'I will have peace, though I walk in the stubbornness of my heart,' so as to sweep away the watered [land] with the dry.
en.B: When such a person hears the words of this oath, they may congratulate themselves in their heart and think, 'I will be safe, even though I follow my own stubborn heart.' That would bring ruin on the watered land and the dry alike.
en.R: Such a person may hear the words of this solemn oath and still feel sure of being blessed. They may think, 'I will be safe, even if I do whatever my stubborn heart wants.' But that would destroy everything, the good with the bad.

es.L: Y sucederá que, cuando oiga las palabras de este juramento, se bendecirá en su corazón, diciendo: “Tendré paz, aunque ande en la terquedad de mi corazón”, para arrasar la [tierra] regada junto con la seca.
es.B: Cuando una persona así oiga las palabras de este juramento, puede felicitarse en su interior y pensar: “Estaré a salvo, aunque siga mi corazón obstinado”. Eso traería la ruina sobre la tierra regada y la seca por igual.
es.R: Esa persona puede oír las palabras de este juramento solemne y aun así sentirse segura de que será bendecida. Puede pensar: “Estaré a salvo aunque haga todo lo que quiera mi terco corazón”. Pero eso lo destruiría todo, lo bueno junto con lo malo.

fr.L: Et il arrivera, quand il entendra les paroles de ce serment, qu’il se bénira dans son cœur en disant : “J’aurai la paix, même si je marche dans l’obstination de mon cœur”, de sorte qu’il emporte la [terre] arrosée avec la sèche.
fr.B: Quand une telle personne entendra les paroles de ce serment, elle risque de se féliciter en elle-même et de penser : “Tout ira bien pour moi, même si je suis mon cœur obstiné.” Cela mènerait à la ruine la terre arrosée comme la terre sèche.
fr.R: Une telle personne peut entendre les paroles de ce serment solennel et se croire quand même bénie. Elle peut penser : “Je serai en sécurité, même si je fais tout ce que veut mon cœur têtu.” Mais cela détruirait tout, le bon avec le mauvais.

sw.L: Na itakuwa, atakaposikia maneno ya kiapo hiki, atajibariki moyoni mwake, akisema, 'Nitakuwa na amani, ingawa ninaenenda katika ukaidi wa moyo wangu,' hata kufagilia mbali [nchi] iliyonyweshwa pamoja na iliyokauka.
sw.B: Mtu wa namna hiyo akisikia maneno ya kiapo hiki, anaweza kujipongeza moyoni mwake na kuwaza, 'Nitakuwa salama, hata nikifuata ukaidi wa moyo wangu.' Jambo hilo lingeleta maangamizi juu ya nchi iliyonyweshwa na iliyokauka vilevile.
sw.R: Mtu kama huyo anaweza kusikia maneno ya kiapo hiki kizito na bado akajiona amebarikiwa. Anaweza kuwaza, 'Nitakuwa salama hata nikifanya chochote ambacho moyo wangu mkaidi unataka.' Lakini hilo lingeangamiza kila kitu, kizuri pamoja na kibaya.

vi.L: Và sẽ xảy ra, khi người ấy nghe các lời của lời thề này, thì nó tự chúc phước cho mình trong lòng, rằng: 'Tôi sẽ được bình an, dù tôi bước đi theo sự cứng cỏi của lòng tôi,' để quét sạch [đất] được tưới cùng với [đất] khô hạn.
vi.B: Khi nghe những lời của lời thề này, người ấy có thể tự chúc mừng mình trong lòng và nghĩ: 'Tôi sẽ được bình an, dù tôi cứ làm theo lòng cứng cỏi của mình.' Điều đó sẽ đem tai họa đến cho cả đất được tưới lẫn đất khô hạn.
vi.R: Người như vậy có thể nghe những lời thề long trọng này mà vẫn yên trí rằng mình sẽ được phước. Người ấy có thể nghĩ: 'Tôi sẽ được an toàn, dù tôi muốn làm gì theo lòng cứng cỏi của mình cũng được.' Nhưng điều đó sẽ hủy hoại tất cả, cả điều tốt lẫn điều xấu.

ko.L: 그리고 그가 이 맹세의 말을 들을 때에 마음속으로 스스로 복을 빌며 '내가 내 마음의 고집대로 걸어도 나에게는 평안이 있을 것이다' 하고 말하여, 물 댄 [땅]과 메마른 [땅]을 함께 쓸어 버리게 될 것이다.
ko.B: 그런 사람은 이 맹세의 말을 듣고도 속으로 스스로를 축하하며 '내가 고집스러운 내 마음대로 살아도 나는 무사할 것이다' 하고 생각할 것이다. 그러면 물 댄 땅과 메마른 땅이 함께 망하게 될 것이다.
ko.R: 그런 사람은 이 엄숙한 맹세의 말을 듣고도 자기는 복을 받을 것이라고 믿을지 모릅니다. 그는 '내 고집대로 무엇이든 해도 나는 괜찮을 것이다' 하고 생각할 것입니다. 그러나 그렇게 하면 좋은 것이든 나쁜 것이든 모든 것이 망하고 말 것입니다.

pt.L: E será que, ao ouvir ele as palavras deste juramento, ele se abençoará no seu coração, dizendo: 'Terei paz, ainda que eu ande na teimosia do meu coração', para varrer a [terra] regada junto com a seca.
pt.B: Quando uma pessoa assim ouvir as palavras deste juramento, ela pode se felicitar no seu íntimo e pensar: 'Nada de mal me acontecerá, mesmo que eu siga o meu coração teimoso.' Isso traria ruína tanto sobre a terra regada como sobre a seca.
pt.R: Essa pessoa pode ouvir as palavras deste juramento solene e mesmo assim ter certeza de que será abençoada. Pode pensar: 'Nada de mal vai me acontecer, mesmo que eu faça tudo o que o meu coração teimoso quiser.' Mas isso destruiria tudo, o bom junto com o ruim.

am.L: እንዲህም ይሆናል፤ የዚህን መሐላ ቃሎች በሰማ ጊዜ በልቡ ራሱን ይባርካል፤ “በልቤ እልከኝነት ብሄድም ሰላም ይሆንልኛል” ይላል፤ ይኸውም የረካውን [ምድር] ከደረቀው ጋር ያጠፋ ዘንድ ነው።
am.B: እንዲህ ያለው ሰው የዚህን መሐላ ቃሎች በሰማ ጊዜ በልቡ ራሱን አጽናንቶ “የገዛ ልቤን እልከኝነት ብከተልም እንኳ ደኅና እሆናለሁ” ብሎ ያስብ ይሆናል። ይህም ውኃ የጠገበውንና ደረቁን ምድር በአንድነት ያጠፋል።
am.R: እንዲህ ያለው ሰው የዚህን ጽኑ መሐላ ቃል ሰምቶ እንኳ እንደሚባረክ እርግጠኛ ሊሆን ይችላል። “እልከኛ ልቤ የፈለገውን ሁሉ ባደርግ እንኳ ደኅና እሆናለሁ” ብሎ ያስብ ይሆናል። ይህ ግን መልካሙን ከክፉው ጋር ሁሉን ያጠፋል።

decisions.choice: bless himself in his heart: tell himself that he is safe
decisions.reason: The verb means to bless oneself, to count oneself blessed. On hearing the curses of the covenant the man assures himself that they will not touch him. "In his heart" means in his own mind, not aloud (Isaiah 65:16; Psalm 49:19).

decisions.choice: peace: safety and well-being; stubbornness: going one's own way against God
decisions.reason: "Peace will be to me" means "all will be well with me" (Jeremiah 23:17). The word for stubbornness is used almost only by Jeremiah (Jeremiah 7:24; 9:13; 13:10), for a heart set on its own way against God's word.

decisions.choice: to sweep away the watered with the dry: probably, to bring ruin on everything
alternatives: it is part of what the man says to himself
the guilty and the innocent alike
decisions.reason: The phrase is hard. "The watered" and "the thirsty" are feminine and probably mean watered and dry ground, a pair that stands for everything together, good and bad alike. On this reading the man's self-deceit brings destruction on the whole land, not on himself alone, as verse 17 warns and verses 21-27 describe. Others take the words to mean adding drunkenness to thirst, or the moist plant with the dry, so that he destroys himself completely. The phrase may also be the man's own words, a careless saying that the rest of his life will go as it will. The text does not decide.

decisions.choice: he ... me: the man or woman of verse 17
decisions.reason: The pronouns are masculine singular, as Hebrew uses for anyone, but they refer back to the person of verse 17, man or woman.

decisions.choice: such a person ... they
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "such a person" and use "they" and "themselves", since verse 17 names a man or a woman. Literal keeps "he" and "his".

decisions.choice: bring ruin on the watered land and the dry alike / destroy everything, the good with the bad
decisions.reason: Balanced follows the likely reading with the words of the picture; Readable gives its meaning in plain words. Both choose the reading in the meaning note, which is uncertain.

decisions.choice: une telle personne ... elle
decisions.reason: Verse 17 names a man or a woman, so Balanced and Readable speak of "une telle personne", which takes "elle" in French without pointing to a woman. Literal keeps "il", as the Hebrew has.

decisions.choice: "그" (L); "그런 사람" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The man or woman of verse 17; Korean "사람" covers both, so Balanced and Readable need no plural "they" as the English does.

decisions.choice: uma pessoa assim ... ela (B); essa pessoa (R); Nada de mal me acontecerá (B, R)
decisions.reason: Verse 17 names a man or a woman (m4), so Balanced and Readable speak of "uma pessoa" and refer back with "ela", as the English says "they"; Literal keeps the Hebrew "ele". "Estarei seguro" would make the speaker a man, so the thought is put as "nada de mal me acontecerá", which says the same safety (m2) for either.

decisions.choice: Amharic "ሰው" with the ordinary masculine verb for "such a person"
decisions.reason: The English Balanced and Readable say "such a person ... they" to cover the man or woman of verse 17. Amharic "ሰው" with the generic masculine already speaks of anyone, so no other wording is needed.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will not be willing to forgive him, for then the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} jealousy will smoke against that man, and every curse written in this book will lie down upon him, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will blot out his name from under heaven.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will not be willing to forgive that person. Instead, the anger and jealousy of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will burn like fire against them, and every curse written in this book will settle on them, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will wipe out their name from under heaven.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will never be willing to forgive that person. The anger and jealousy of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will blaze up against them. Every curse written in this book will fall on them, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will wipe out every memory of them from the earth.

es.L: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no querrá perdonarlo, porque entonces humeará la ira {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} celo contra ese hombre, y toda maldición escrita en este libro se echará sobre él, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} borrará su nombre de debajo del cielo.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no querrá perdonar a esa persona. Al contrario, la ira y el celo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} arderán como fuego contra ella, todas las maldiciones escritas en este libro se asentarán sobre ella, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} borrará su nombre de debajo del cielo.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nunca querrá perdonar a esa persona. La ira y el celo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} se encenderán contra ella. Todas las maldiciones escritas en este libro caerán sobre ella, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} borrará de la tierra todo recuerdo de ella.

fr.L: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne voudra pas lui pardonner, car alors la colère {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} jalousie fumeront contre cet homme, et toute la malédiction écrite dans ce livre se couchera sur lui, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} effacera son nom de dessous le ciel.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne voudra pas pardonner à cette personne. Au contraire, la colère et la jalousie {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} s’enflammeront contre elle, toutes les malédictions écrites dans ce livre reposeront sur elle, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} effacera son nom de dessous le ciel.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne voudra jamais pardonner à cette personne. La colère et la jalousie {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} s’embraseront contre elle. Toutes les malédictions écrites dans ce livre tomberont sur elle, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} effacera de la terre tout souvenir d’elle.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hatakuwa radhi kumsamehe, kwa maana hapo hasira ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na wivu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} vitafuka moshi juu ya mtu huyo, na laana yote iliyoandikwa katika kitabu hiki italala juu yake, na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atalifuta jina lake kutoka chini ya mbingu.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hatakubali kumsamehe mtu huyo. Badala yake, hasira na wivu wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} vitawaka kama moto juu yake, kila laana iliyoandikwa katika kitabu hiki itatua juu yake, na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atalifuta jina lake chini ya mbingu.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hatakubali kamwe kumsamehe mtu huyo. Hasira na wivu wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} vitawaka juu yake. Kila laana iliyoandikwa katika kitabu hiki itamwangukia, na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atafuta kabisa kumbukumbu lake duniani.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ không muốn tha thứ cho nó, vì khi ấy cơn giận của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và sự kỵ tà của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ bốc khói nghịch lại người ấy, mọi sự nguyền rủa đã chép trong sách này sẽ nằm trên nó, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ xóa tên nó khỏi dưới trời.
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ không chịu tha thứ cho người ấy. Trái lại, cơn giận và sự kỵ tà của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ bừng cháy nghịch lại người ấy, mọi sự nguyền rủa đã chép trong sách này sẽ đổ xuống và ở lại trên người ấy, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ xóa tên người ấy khỏi dưới trời.
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ không bao giờ chịu tha thứ cho người ấy. Cơn giận và sự kỵ tà của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ bùng lên nghịch lại người ấy. Mọi sự nguyền rủa đã chép trong sách này sẽ giáng trên người ấy, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ xóa sạch mọi ký ức về người ấy khỏi mặt đất.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 그를 용서하려 하지 않으실 것이니, 그때에 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 분노와 그분의 질투가 그 사람에게 연기를 뿜을 것이고, 이 책에 기록된 모든 저주가 그 위에 내려앉을 것이며, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그의 이름을 하늘 아래에서 지워 버리실 것이다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 그런 사람을 결코 용서하지 않으실 것이다. 오히려 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 분노와 질투가 불처럼 그 사람에게 타오르고, 이 책에 기록된 모든 저주가 그에게 내려 머물 것이며, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그의 이름을 하늘 아래에서 지워 버리실 것이다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 그런 사람을 결코 용서하지 않으실 것입니다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그 사람에게 몹시 노하시고 질투하실 것입니다. 이 책에 적힌 모든 저주가 그에게 내릴 것이고, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 그 사람을 기억하는 이가 이 땅에 아무도 없게 하실 것입니다.

pt.L: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} não quererá perdoá-lo, porque então fumegará a ira {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} e o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} zelo contra aquele homem, e se deitará sobre ele toda a maldição escrita neste livro, e {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} apagará o nome dele de debaixo do céu.
pt.B: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} não estará disposto a perdoar essa pessoa. Pelo contrário, a ira e o zelo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} arderão como fogo contra ela, toda a maldição escrita neste livro recairá sobre ela, e {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} apagará o nome dela de debaixo do céu.
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} nunca vai querer perdoar essa pessoa. A ira e o zelo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} vão se acender contra ela como um fogo. Todas as maldições escritas neste livro vão cair sobre ela, e {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} vai apagar da terra toda lembrança dela.

am.L: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ይቅር ሊለው አይፈቅድም፤ ያን ጊዜ {{divine_name:የእግዚአብሔር|የያህዌ}} ቁጣና ቅንዓቱ በዚያ ሰው ላይ ይጤሳል፤ በዚህ መጽሐፍ የተጻፈውም እርግማን ሁሉ በእርሱ ላይ ይተኛል፤ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}}ም ስሙን ከሰማይ በታች ይደመስሳል።
am.B: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ያንን ሰው ይቅር ሊለው አይፈቅድም። ይልቁንም {{divine_name:የእግዚአብሔር|የያህዌ}} ቁጣና ቅንዓት እንደ እሳት በእርሱ ላይ ይነድዳል፤ በዚህ መጽሐፍ የተጻፈውም እርግማን ሁሉ በእርሱ ላይ ያርፋል፤ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}}ም ስሙን ከሰማይ በታች ይደመስሳል።
am.R: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ያንን ሰው ፈጽሞ ይቅር አይለውም። {{divine_name:የእግዚአብሔር|የያህዌ}} ቁጣና ቅንዓት በእርሱ ላይ ይነድዳል። በዚህ መጽሐፍ የተጻፈው እርግማን ሁሉ ይደርስበታል፤ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}}ም ከምድር ላይ መታሰቢያውን ሁሉ ያጠፋል።

decisions.choice: the anger of the LORD will smoke: his anger will flare up
decisions.reason: Anger is pictured as fire and its smoke, as in Psalm 74:1 and 80:5. "Jealousy" is God's zeal for the loyalty he is owed, the jealousy of 4:24 and 5:9, which will not share his people with other gods.

decisions.choice: every curse ... will lie down on him: the curses will settle on him and stay
decisions.reason: The word translated "curse" is the same as "oath" in verses 11, 13 and 18: the oath brings its curses on whoever breaks it. "Lie down" is used of an animal crouching at rest (Genesis 49:9); the curses come to rest on the man and do not leave.

decisions.choice: blot out his name from under heaven: leave no one and nothing to remember him
decisions.reason: A person's name lived on in his descendants and in the memory of his people. To blot it out is to end his line and his memory completely (9:14; 25:6, 19; Exodus 17:14).

decisions.choice: will not be willing to forgive: will refuse to pardon
decisions.reason: The man who hoped to be safe (verse 18) will find no pardon. The same verb is used in 1:26 of Israel's refusal to go up into the land and in 10:10 of the LORD's unwillingness to destroy them.

decisions.choice: that person ... them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable continue from verse 18 with "that person" and "they", since a man or a woman is meant (verse 17). Literal keeps "that man" and "him", as the Hebrew has.

decisions.choice: burn like fire
decisions.reason: Balanced says "burn like fire" for "smoke", keeping the picture of fire without the unusual verb. Readable says "blaze up".

decisions.choice: wipe out every memory of them from the earth
decisions.reason: Readable says what blotting out a name means, and "from the earth" for "from under heaven", everywhere people live.

decisions.choice: "sự kỵ tà" for the LORD's jealousy (qin'ah)
decisions.reason: The settled word for the jealous God (qanna) is "kỵ tà"; the noun follows it.

decisions.choice: "질투"
decisions.reason: As the Pentateuch's choice for the LORD's jealousy (Exodus 20:5 in Korean): the burning claim of God on his own people.

decisions.choice: o zelo
decisions.reason: God's "jealousy" is "zelo", the noun of "Deus zeloso" in 4:24 and 5:9 (m1): his zeal for the loyalty he is owed. "Ciúme" in Portuguese suggests a petty, possessive feeling.

records.literal_gloss: And will separate him Yahweh for evil from all [the] tribes of Israel according to all [the] oaths of the covenant the written in [the] book of the law the this.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will set him apart for harm from all the tribes of Israel, according to all the curses of the covenant written in this book of the law.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will single them out from all the tribes of Israel for disaster, in keeping with all the covenant curses written in this book of the law.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will pick that person out from all the tribes of Israel to be punished. It will happen just as all the curses of the covenant in this book of teaching say.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo apartará para el mal de entre todas las tribus de Israel, conforme a todas las maldiciones del pacto escritas en este libro de la ley.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} apartará a esa persona de entre todas las tribus de Israel para la desgracia, conforme a todas las maldiciones del pacto escritas en este libro de la ley.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} escogerá a esa persona de entre todas las tribus de Israel para castigarla. Sucederá tal como dicen todas las maldiciones del pacto que están en este libro de enseñanza.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} le séparera de toutes les tribus d’Israël pour le malheur, selon toutes les malédictions de l’alliance écrites dans ce livre de la loi.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} mettra cette personne à part, parmi toutes les tribus d’Israël, pour la frapper de malheur, conformément à toutes les malédictions de l’alliance écrites dans ce livre de la loi.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} choisira cette personne parmi toutes les tribus d’Israël pour la punir. Tout se passera comme le disent les malédictions de l’alliance écrites dans ce livre d’enseignement.

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atamtenga kwa ajili ya mabaya kutoka katika makabila yote ya Israeli, kwa kufuata laana zote za agano zilizoandikwa katika kitabu hiki cha sheria.
